title: When the Playlist Sings
premise: Elodie Galloway, a seventeen-year-old coder who has spent a decade hiding behind an anonymous account that exposes corruption, finds coded instructions in her late grandmother's recipe box—directions that reveal her grandmother ran the same vigilante network Elodie unknowingly inherited. As she deciphers the recipes, she discovers the network's remaining members are being hunted by the man her grandmother once brought down, and every message she sends online tightens his grip. With prom approaching and her found family of misfit friends pulled into the danger, Elodie must choose between staying invisible and finishing what her grandmother started, culminating in a public unmasking at prom where she trades her anonymity for justice—and finally learns who she is when the labels come off.
about_author: Quentin Whitlock is a former radio DJ turned novelist who writes stories about kids who are louder in text than they are in person. He lives in a coastal town full of diners, dead frequencies, and excellent playlists.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. We meet her double life: quiet scholarship student by day, anonymous whistleblower 'staticgirl' by night. She posts evidence that sinks a local developer, then panics and scrubs everything. Emotional beat: control as armor, and the loneliness it costs.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Clearing out grandma Ruthie's kitchen, Elodie finds cards with impossible ingredients—'one part ledger, bake until the bank folds.' The last card bears a username she recognizes from old forums: staticgirl wasn't Ruthie's first successor. Beat: grief cracking open into wonder.

chapters.title: Sourdough Starter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She tests the first recipe against city archives and confirms Ruthie exposed a 1980s loan scandal. Her best friend Dev, a conspiracy-brained theater kid, notices her distraction. Beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by fear of what inheriting this means.

chapters.title: The Diner Regulars
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev drags Elodie to the Blue Plate Diner, where three elderly regulars—Miss Okafor, Hank, and Ruthie's old friend Pearl—watch them too closely. Elodie realizes they're testing her. Beat: found family forming around a shared secret she doesn't fully hold yet.

chapters.title: Card Fourteen: Burn After Reading
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A recipe card instructs her to retrieve a hidden drive; inside is proof that Councilman Voss—the developer she exposed—has been hunting Ruthie's network for years, and he's closing in on Pearl. Beat: the game turns lethal; curiosity becomes obligation.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Prom planning collides with investigation as Voss's daughter Marisol, sharp-tongued and observant, joins the committee and starts asking why Elodie keeps leaving meetings early. Beat: the two worlds threaten to merge; first sparks of an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: What Pearl Knows
chapters.summary: Pearl's POV (flashback woven in). Pearl reveals Ruthie built the network after losing her bakery to the same men Voss now serves, and that Ruthie chose Elodie deliberately. Beat: inheritance reframed—not a burden dropped on her, but trust placed in her.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Someone replies to staticgirl's dormant account using Ruthie's private phrases. It's a trap or a test. Elodie traces the ping to a server tied to Voss's firm. Beat: paranoia; the price of survival is realizing you were never actually safe.

chapters.title: The Lock-In
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. A school lock-in becomes cover for Elodie to copy files from the administration server, which Voss has been quietly accessing through a district contract. Marisol catches her—and covers for her. Beat: unexpected loyalty from the least likely ally.

chapters.title: Marisol Voss Doesn't Flinch
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol admits she's suspected her father for a year; his money bought their house and her silence. She offers Elodie access to his home office. Beat: two girls choosing each other over blood and brand names.

chapters.title: Hank's Hands Shake
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Hank, the diner cook, is followed home and beaten—a warning aimed at the network. In the hospital, he presses a key into Elodie's palm. Beat: guilt and fury; survival has a body count, and it's people she loves.

chapters.title: Everything I Baked for You
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Deciphering the final recipe cards, Elodie finds Ruthie's letter: an apology for leaving her the war, and permission to walk away. Beat: the emotional core—love that lets go, and a choice made freely rather than by duty.

chapters.title: Walk Away
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Elodie tries to quit—deletes the account, burns the cards' copies, plans a normal prom. But Voss escalates, framing Miss Okafor for embezzlement to flush out the network. Beat: the false peace before the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Watching Okafor arrested, Elodie understands invisibility was always someone else's win. She rebuilds staticgirl with one purpose: not leaks, but a public reckoning timed to prom night, when the whole town will be watching. Beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The crew rehearses the plan: Marisol gets Voss's laptop, Dev handles the AV rig, Pearl distracts security, Elodie broadcasts. Every step has a failure mode. Beat: tension braided with tenderness—they've become a family under fire.

chapters.title: Prom Night: Slow Song
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The gym glitters; Voss arrives to give a speech. Marisol plants the drive. For one song, Elodie lets herself dance with Dev and pretend. Beat: the calmest chapter, deliberately—happiness held like breath before the plunge.

chapters.title: Feedback Loop
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Mid-speech, the screens hijack: ledgers, recordings, Ruthie's face. Voss spots Marisol's trembling hands and realizes. Chaos erupts as he moves toward the AV booth. Beat: climax ignites; the plan works and immediately unravels.

chapters.title: Behind the Booth
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Voss corners Elodie and Dev; he offers her money, then threats, revealing he killed Ruthie's partner decades ago. Elodie stalls him while police—tipped by Okafor's lawyer—arrive. Beat: terror transmuted into defiance; she speaks truth to his face, unmasked.

chapters.title: The Whole Gym Sees Her
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Handcuffed, Voss spits her name—'the little hacker girl'—and instead of shame, Elodie stands up in her prom dress and owns it. The crowd's silence turns to applause. Beat: catharsis; anonymity dies and identity is born in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Extra Frosting
chapters.summary: Pearl's POV. The diner reopens; charges against Okafor drop; Voss awaits trial. Pearl gives Elodie Ruthie's original recipe box, empty now except for one new card Pearl wrote: 'Start something of your own.' Beat: mourning softens into gratitude.

chapters.title: What Staticgirl Does Next
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Reporters circle, colleges call, and Elodie decides staticgirl won't be an anonymous ghost anymore but a named collective—her, Dev, Marisol, Pearl—doing careful, accountable work. Beat: purpose chosen, not inherited; the price of survival paid forward.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. Summer. On the diner's old jukebox, Elodie queues the song from prom and dances badly with her people while a new recipe card waits in her pocket—her own handwriting, her own fight. Beat: joy earned; the playlist sings because she finally does.
